page.layout: One printed page, text in a single column on the right of the scan; a fragment of the facing page's text lies in the narrow strip at the far left, which is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. Below the column: a verse epigram in italic, a date line, a signature line in larger type, a printer's ornament, and a signature letter B at the foot.

main_text.p: riis, Arianis, Samosatenianis, & qui idge- nus erat, publicè in Universi huius amphi- theatro, scriptis congressi, etiam cominus, pugnarunt. Meum calculum si requiras, pervelim, (ita meum votum habet) & necessarium, atque ex re Ecclesiæ existimo, TUUM SCRIPTUM publicitùs legi. Valeᵗ, mi LUCI oculissime; & quà Gry- næus desinet, Tu aciem instrue, ducito, pugna: & triumphum in cælis exspecta, adoreà cingendus immarcescibili.

p.i: Norimb. 6. Eid. Martias. cIↄ.Iↄ c. x.

page.notes: Small printer's ornament (a heart-shaped fleuron) between the Remus signature and the foot; not transcribed. The date reads cIↄ.Iↄ c. x. as printed, i.e. MDCX. The line "Tuus fide fidâ, nexu mancupI," is set in larger type and is treated as a paragraph, not a heading. Show-through of text from the reverse side is visible in the middle of the page and is not transcribed. The text at the far left edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.
